method: scripts/ib-research/claim-check.js: the passage is copied verbatim from the live source text at the pinned revision; VERIFIED = every claim number in one sentence that shares >= 50% of the claim's content words

records.claim: The lunar distance is approximately 385,000 km, or 1.3 light-seconds.
records.passage: The semi-major axis of the geocentric lunar orbit, called the lunar distance, is approximately 385,000 km (239,000 mi), or 1.3 light-seconds, comparable to going around Earth approximately 9.6 times.

records.claim: The speed of gravitational waves equals the speed of light, confirmed by observation of the GW170817 neutron star merger.
records.passage: In the relativistic sense, the "speed of gravity" refers to the speed of a gravitational wave, which, as predicted by general relativity and confirmed by observation of the GW170817 neutron star merger, is equal to the speed of light (c).

records.claim: The Sun's tides have a theoretical amplitude of about 25 centimetres, 46% of that of the Moon.
records.passage: The Sun similarly causes tides, of which the theoretical amplitude is about 25 centimetres (9.8 in) (46% of that of the Moon) with a cycle time of 12 hours.

records.claim: Earth currently has an axial tilt of about 23.44°.
records.passage: Earth currently has an axial tilt of about 23.44°.

records.claim: Numerical simulations in 2011 indicated that even without the Moon, Earth's obliquity might vary only by about 20–25°.
records.passage: However, more recent numerical simulations made in 2011 indicated that even in the absence of the Moon, Earth's obliquity might not be quite so unstable; varying only by about 20–25°.

narration.text: If the Moon vanished, tides wouldn't stop.
The Sun still raises tides about 46% as strong.
And gravity's news travels only at light speed.
The Moon is 1.3 light-seconds away, so Earth notices 1.3 seconds later.
Then the big lunar tides fade, leaving the smaller solar ones.
Earth's tilt, now 23.44 degrees, loses a stabilizer.
But 2011 simulations suggest it might only wander between 20 and 25 degrees.
So the first change you'd see is darker nights.
